requirement: Reaching and completing an expression are distinguished

obligations.note: the division starts evaluating (reached) but raises a runtime division-by-zero error before the assignment to result completes. A tool that only distinguishes reached vs. not-reached will (correctly) call this line hit; a tool that additionally claims the assignment succeeded would be wrong.
never reached: the function aborts on line 4's error, so the return statement never executes

notes: Divisor 0 is passed as a variable, not a literal -- `100 / 0` written directly is caught at parse/constant-fold time (a SCRIPT ERROR before the script even loads), which is a different, uninteresting failure mode. Routing the zero through a parameter forces a genuine runtime error inside a running function, confirmed on the pinned Godot 4.7.1 engine via pilot/fixtures/driver.gd: the error aborts only the run() call (prints SCRIPT ERROR to stderr), the caller is unaffected, and GDScript coerces the aborted call's return value to the declared type's default (int -> 0). This distinguishes 'reached' (line 4 started executing) from 'completed' (the assignment and the following return never happen).
author: godot-tooling-session-2026-09-19
ambiguities: Only one error type (division by zero) is exercised. Other runtime errors that can occur mid-expression (null method calls, out-of-bounds indexing, type-cast failures) are assumed to abort the same way but are not individually tested.
